title: The Clean Break Hour with Ronnie
description: Ronnie answers listener letters about grief, retirement, and starting over with serene total confidence and one fix for everything: box it up, put it in the garage. Barry is the only one who notices.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's The Clean Break Hour, where every heavy heart leaves a little lighter. Maureen writes, my husband of forty years passed, and I can't sleep on my side of the bed.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Maureen, easy fix. Box up his side of the bed, label it, and pop it in the garage.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie... a marriage is not clutter.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Clutter has feelings too, Barry. Last one. Read Priya's letter.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She says, I moved across the country for a fresh start, and now I'm grieving the life I left behind.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Priya, that's just unboxed feelings rattling around. Box up the old city, label it, and leave it in a garage you no longer own.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't box a city, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You can if you believe, Barry. <p:0.3> Cardboard does the rest.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: New letter, Ronnie. Maureen took your advice. Boxed up his side of the bed... and now sleeps in the garage to be near him.
